In algebraic geometry, the '''abundance conjecture''' is a conjecture in 
[[birational geometry]], more precisely in the [[minimal model program]],
stating that for every [[projective variety]] <math>X</math> with [[Kawamata log terminal singularity|Kawamata log terminal singularities]] over a field <math>k</math> if the [[canonical bundle]] <math>K_X</math> is [[Nef line bundle|nef]], then <math>K_X</math> is [[Ample_line_bundle|semi-ample]], i.e. <math>mK_X</math> is base-point free for some <math>m>0</math>. In particular, if abundance holds, then one is able to define a model <math>X\rightarrow Y=\mathrm{Proj}\bigoplus_{l\geqslant 0} H^0(X, lK_X).</math>

Important cases of the abundance conjecture have been proven by [[Caucher Birkar]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1007/s10240-012-0039-5|title = Existence of log canonical flips and a special LMMP| journal=Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS| volume=115| pages=325–368|year = 2012|last1 = Birkar|first1 = Caucher| arxiv=1104.4981}}</ref>
